sanity_expectations: Q > 0 and finite everywhere in the sampled region
At fixed T_body, Q rises then falls with M (sub-linear M**alpha growth capped by supply saturation), peaking near M ~ M_sat
Mass-specific rate Q/M decreases with increasing M (larger organisms have lower per-unit-mass metabolism)
Maintenance surcharge (1+Q_maint*M**-gamma) inflates Q most at the smallest masses
At fixed M, Q is suppressed for T_body below T_low (~280 K) and above T_deact (~315 K)
The temperature Arrhenius-like factor equals 1 exactly at T_body = T_ref = 298 K
excitation_report: Expression is a single top-level product term: rms 0.692 = 34.6*sigma (visible). NEW low-temperature suppression factor (1+(T_low/T_body)**epsilon)**(-1): max effect 3.52 = 176.1*sigma, strongest at M~4.16 kg, T_body~266 K (just below T_low=280 K, where cold-induced depression is strongest). Parent's high-T deactivation factor is also exercised because T_body range reaches 320 K > T_deact=315 K. All terms pass >=5*sigma; weak_terms empty.
role_corrections: Q: output->dependent variable (confirmed; explicitly solvable, appears on LHS only)
M: input axis->independent variable (confirmed; body mass, log-sampled over 6 decades)
T_body: input axis->independent variable (confirmed; must be sampled, not fixed, or the NEW low-T term and parent's high-T deactivation term degenerate to constants)
E_a: P->P (confirmed; kept small so the non-standard temperature factor stays bounded)
k_B: P->P (confirmed; physical Boltzmann constant in eV/K)
rationale: analyze_expression confirms an explicit, algebraic relation (no derivatives/integrals; target solvable), so type=explicit, integrator=evaluate_explicit. M and T_body are the two sampling axes; all 13 other symbols are fixed parameters (T_low, epsilon taken from the suggested ranges). M spans 0.001-1000 kg on a log scale to capture cross-species allometry and the M_sat supply-saturation crossover; T_body spans 265-320 K to cross both the NEW low-temperature suppression (T_low=280 K) and the parent high-temperature deactivation (T_deact=315 K). E_a is set to 4.3085e-3 eV (E_a/k_B ~ 50 K) because the given non-standard temperature factor (T_body/T_ref)**((E_a/k_B)*(1-T_ref/T_body)) blows up for literature-scale activation energies over this range; the chosen value keeps Q finite (verified 0.61 at the reference point, 0.012 at an extreme) while remaining a small positive activation energy. sigma=0.02 (small vs the ~0.1-3 dependent-variable scale); excitation_check confirms every term, and the new low-T term at 176*sigma, is visible.

scenario_text: A physiologist examines how oxygen consumption rate of resting animals scales across species of very different body mass. Larger organisms consume more oxygen in total but less per unit mass, reflecting integrated metabolic organization. The measurement is taken under standardized resting conditions. We seek the resting whole-organism metabolic rate as a function of body mass.
